question: Should OpenClaw adopt earliest-layer path ownership with narrowly defined monotonic `tools.allow` and `tools.deny` exceptions as its permanent opt-in managed-configuration contract?
rationale: This establishes who controls configuration values and which later policy changes are considered security-tightening; tests can verify an implementation but cannot choose that product and trust model.

options.title: Keep Draft Pending Contract Review
options.body: Retain draft status while maintainers review precedence, write behavior, diagnostics, and the closed set of security-tightening exceptions.

options.title: Accept The V1 Contract
options.body: Approve the described opt-in semantics, create the implementation issue, change the RFC to accepted, and coordinate landing with the linked OpenClaw PR.

options.title: Retain Host-Side Composition
options.body: Decline a core layering contract and continue treating managed overlays as host or deployment integration responsibility.

recommendation.title: Keep Draft Pending Contract Review
recommendation.body: Retain draft status while maintainers review precedence, write behavior, diagnostics, and the closed set of security-tightening exceptions.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision changes a cross-cutting core configuration and security contract, and the project lead is the strongest available product-direction owner.
